description: A minecraft server-side fabric mod intended to increase the stakes of a multiplayer minecraft playthrough by removing several features usually taken for granted and provide an overall more immersive experience.

mods.name: YOLT Anvils
mods.description: Server-side flat anvil prices: each use costs the price of its biggest job, using an item again never makes it dearer, and nothing is ever too expensive. Set the prices in config/yolt-anvils.json. Also part of You Only Live Twice.

mods.name: You Only Live Twice
mods.description: Server-side hardcore multiplayer: dying locks you out for days, your items wait in a grave anyone can loot, a logout leaves your body behind, and the server hides who is online.

releases.notes:
YOLT 1.2.1 for Minecraft 26.3. It's a server-side Fabric mod: players join with a plain vanilla client and no client
mod.

This release closes five ways a player's client could learn what YOLT hides, fixes a set of bugs found in two audits,
adds settings for YOLT's texts and more, and makes the flat anvil price a mod of its own. No default changes.

## Hidden information: five leaks closed

- **Lodestone compasses in sign and head text.** A compass shown in the hover text of a sign, a hanging sign or a
  player head carried its real target. Those blocks now go through the coordinate offset too.
- **The decimals of a position.** A shifted position could keep enough of its decimals to work the offset out. Shifted
  positions are now rounded onto a fixed grid.
- **The world seed hash.** Every client got the real one. Each connection now gets its own made-up hash; admin view
  still gets the real one.
- **A pet's death message.** It reached the pet's owner even with game messages hidden. Now only in admin view, or
  with `hide.gameMessages` off.
- **"The server is full."** A refused join said the server was full, which tells how many are online. It now says
  "You can't join right now. Try again later." (`messages.serverFull`).

## Fixes

- A fall that lands right after another hit is judged whole, so it still breaks legs.
- The Curse of the Undead never takes your last heart, whatever else raised your maximum health.
- A cake slice counts only the part of it that fits your food bar toward your nutrients.
- The blood moon blocks the night skip from its warning on, not only once it has risen.
- A lockout's wait can't grow past its cooldown if the server's clock is set back, and a body's logout time is fixed
  the same way.
- A logout saves the body file at once, and a failed write is tried again at the next save.
- An item that can't be saved is left out of a grave or a body, instead of the whole file failing to save.
- A hardcore state that couldn't be read is never saved over.
- One slowdown that fails no longer stops the others.
- At most 16 skin lookups wait on Mojang at once.
- Revive papers follow a changed `resourcePack.reviveModel`.
- `/yolt reload` fails cleanly when it can't keep a copy of an older config.
- `hardcore.slow.cap` can be 0, which turns every slowdown off.

## New settings

- **`messages`:** the 15 texts YOLT tells players can be reworded, from the lockout screens and `/help` to the grave
  lines, the revive paper's name, the grave menu's title and the blood moon lines. `/yolt config messages.<key>
  <text>` sets one in game.
- **`allowedCommands`:** more commands a non-op keeps while `restrictCommands` is on, such as another mod's `vote`.
- **`hide.tabHeaderFrame`:** turn off the grey rows of dashes around the tab list header.
- **`hardcore.curse.afkMinutes`:** with `countAfk` off, how long a player may stand idle before curse time stops.
- **`hardcore.bloodMoon.barColour`:** the blood moon boss bar's colour.

The [config documentation](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/docs/config.md) has the
details.

## Faster

- Carried weight is no longer worked out from scratch every tally, so shulkers full of bundles stop costing the server
  time.
- Graves are found by chunk, bodies by their entity, and mobs skip the body search when no body is loaded.
- Less work per packet for the coordinate offset, and one body file write when the server stops.

## YOLT Anvils, a mod of its own

The flat anvil price is now also `yolt-anvils-1.2.1.jar`, for a Fabric server that wants only that part. On its own
it reads `config/yolt-anvils.json` and gives ops `/yolt-anvils reload`. YOLT's own jar already holds it and sets it from
`hardcore.anvil`, so a YOLT server needs nothing extra. Its
[readme](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/anvil/README.md) has the rest.

## What it does

- **Death lockout.** Dying kicks you, and you can't rejoin for 7 days (configurable).

releases.notes:
YOLT 1.2.0 for Minecraft 26.3. It's a server-side Fabric mod: players join with a plain vanilla client and no client
mod.

## What's new: a flavour MOTD

- **The server list shows a flavour line as the MOTD.** A new one each time a player refreshes the list, never the
  same one twice in a row. The lines are `serverList.motdLines` in the config. By default they are the 13 lines of
  the tab list header, colours and all. A line can hold one `\n` to fill both rows of the MOTD.
- **A server updating to 1.2.0 gets it too**, since the new key arrives at its default. To keep your own MOTD from
  `server.properties`, set `"motdLines": []` in the `serverList` section and run `/yolt reload`.
- Only the server list's normal ping shows the line. Clients older than 1.7, the query port (`enable-query`) and the
  game itself after a join get the MOTD from `server.properties`.

The [config documentation](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/docs/config.md#serverlist)
has the details.

`/status` is easier to read, with colour and shorter lines.

## What it does

- **Death lockout.** Dying kicks you, and you can't rejoin for 7 days (configurable).
- **Graves.** Your items stay in a player head where you died, and anyone can loot it. Graves can't be broken and
  never expire.
- **Reviving.** Craft a grave head with a nether star, a netherite ingot, a diamond, a gold ingot and an iron ingot
  into a paper called "Revive <name>". Right-click with it to end that player's lockout.
- **Logout bodies.** When you log out, your body stays where you stood. Whatever happens to it happens to you.
- **Hidden information.** Global chat becomes proximity chat. The tab list, nametags, commands, the online player
  count, death, join and advancement messages and the coordinates on F3 are hidden. The server list shows no names
  and a flavour MOTD. Ops can turn on an admin view to see all of it.
- **World border.** The Overworld and the Nether share one border, 10,000 blocks across by default, with no Nether
  fast travel. New players spawn at a random spot inside it.
- **Hardcore layer.** Extra rules that make survival itself harder, each with its own switch. The Curse of the
  Undead, the flat anvil price and the Mending nerf are on by default. The rest is off until you turn it on.

The [documentation](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/docs/README.md) explains each feature.

## Install

You need Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1 or newer, Fabric API 0.165.2+26.3 or newer, and Java 25.

Put the jar in the server's `mods` folder next to Fabric API and start the server once. It writes the config and,
with the world border on (the default), sets the border to 10,000 blocks across.

Updating from 1.1.0 needs nothing else. At its next start the config file gets `serverList.motdLines` at its default.
The log doesn't name it, since the file's layout (`configVersion` 2) is the same. Going back to 1.1.0 is safe: it
warns that `serverList.motdLines` is an unknown key and leaves it out of the file.

Updating from 1.0.0 needs nothing else either:

- The old config is kept as `you-only-live-twice.json.v1.bak`, and the file goes to `configVersion` 2.
- `hide.coordinates`, `chat.allowWhispers` and `skins.lockAfterFirstChoice` are turned on only where your file still
  says `false`, 1.0.0's default. Each one turned on gets a line in the log with the command to turn it off again, such
  as `/yolt config hide.coordinates false`. One you already set to `true` stays.
- The keys and sections 1.0.0 didn't have are added at their defaults, and the log names them. So the flavour MOTD,
  the Curse of the Undead, the flat anvil price and the Mending nerf come on too.
- 1.0.0 leaves the newer config alone if you go back, since it is from a newer version.

## Good to know

- Revive papers can get their own look from a resource pack, `you-only-live-twice-revive-pack-1.2.0.zip` on this

releases.notes:
YOLT 1.1.0 for Minecraft 26.3. It's a server-side Fabric mod: players join with a plain vanilla client and no client
mod.

## What's new: the hardcore layer

A set of optional rules that make survival itself harder. Each part has its own switch, and with a part off nothing
changes for it. **Only the Curse of the Undead, the flat anvil price and the Mending nerf are on by default**, so every
player now has `/status`, with a Rules line. The rest is off until you turn it on.

- **Weight.** Everything you carry weighs something, and a heavy load slows you down. Armour and tools barely count:
  your kit and half an inventory of ordinary blocks still walk at full speed, and shulker boxes full of stone are half
  speed.
- **Broken legs.** A long fall breaks your legs and slows you until they heal.
- **Limp.** Very low health slows you.
- **Bed rest.** Lying in a bed heals you, day or night.
- **Curse of the Undead.** Each return from death, by dying or by a totem, costs a max heart. They come back with play
  time.
- **Nutrients.** Foods carry protein, vitamins and sugar, and running low on one costs you. One simple food never
  covers all three: eat two or three kinds, or rabbit stew.
- **Hunger tax, Mending nerf, flat anvil prices and an elytra nerf.**
- **Tougher and relentless mobs.** More health, harder hits, a longer chase, and zombies that break doors.
- **Blood moons.** Some nights bring more, tougher and better geared mobs that drop more.
- **Cold.** Out in the snow a chill builds, and torches, fires and leather keep it off.
- **`/status`** shows each player a report on their own body.
- **The curse can outlast the limp.** A server may let the curse take a player low enough to limp until a heart comes
  back; the log only notes it.
- **Revive paper texture.** Revive papers can get their own look from a resource pack (a placeholder texture for
  now). The pack is `you-only-live-twice-revive-pack-1.1.0.zip` on this release. YOLT doesn't send it: host it and set
  it in `server.properties`.

The [hardcore documentation](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/docs/hardcore.md) explains
each part and how to set up the pack.

## New defaults

- `hide.coordinates` is on: every player sees X and Z shifted by a private amount.
- `chat.allowWhispers` is on: everyone can `/w` a player in range.
- `skins.lockAfterFirstChoice` is on: a player picks their skin once, then only an op changes it.
- `hardcore.anvil.enabled` and `hardcore.mending.enabled` are on.
- `hardcore.curse.enabled` is on: the Curse of the Undead. Each return from death, by dying or by a totem, costs a
  max heart, up to 4, and one comes back after every 3 Minecraft days (60 minutes) of play. A server updating from
  1.0.0 gets it too. To turn it off: `/yolt config hardcore.curse.enabled false`.
- `hardcore.legs.bodiesCanBreakLegs` is off: a logout body's fall only costs it health. Nothing about a logged-out
  player heals, so legs broken then would stay broken until they came back.

## Other changes

- **Whispers are logged.** Each whisper writes one line to the server log: who sent it, to which name, the text and
  whether it was heard. Players see nothing new.
- **One whisper for every player.** `/msg` and `/tell` are now the same ranged whisper as `/w` for players, ops too,
  so no player can reach another out of earshot. The console, command blocks and datapack functions keep vanilla's
  `/msg`, `/tell` and `/w`, selectors and all. `/teammsg` stays vanilla.
- **Nether portals at 1:1 link only nearby.** A Nether portal looks for an Overworld portal within 16 blocks of its
  exit, not 128, so it can't lead to someone else's base. A pair that linked further apart makes a new portal once.
- **The flat anvil clears the counter.** Every item that comes out of an anvil while the flat price is on has
  vanilla's hidden prior-work counter at 0, so it prices like a new item if the flat price is turned off.

releases.notes:
YOLT for Minecraft 26.3. It's a server-side Fabric mod: players join with a plain vanilla client, no client mod and no
resource pack.

## What it does

- **Death lockout.** Dying kicks you, and you can't rejoin for 7 days (configurable).
- **Graves.** Your items stay in a player head where you died, and anyone can loot it. Graves can't be broken and
  never expire.
- **Reviving.** Craft a grave head with a nether star, a netherite ingot, a diamond, a gold ingot and an iron ingot
  into a paper called "Revive <name>". Right-click with it to end that player's lockout.
- **Logout bodies.** When you log out, your body stays where you stood. Whatever happens to it happens to you.
- **Hidden information.** Global chat becomes proximity chat. The tab list, nametags, commands, the online player
  count, death, join and advancement messages and the coordinates on F3 are hidden. Ops can turn on an admin view to
  see all of it.
- **World border.** The Overworld and the Nether share one border, 10,000 blocks across by default, with no Nether
  fast travel. New players spawn at a random spot inside it.
- **Off by default:** a grave compass that points at your latest grave, and fake X and Z coordinates for each player
  (`hide.coordinates`).

Every feature has a switch in `config/you-only-live-twice.json`, and `/yolt config` changes them in game. The
[documentation](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/docs/README.md) explains each one.

## Install

You need Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.20.1 or newer, Fabric API 0.165.2+26.3 or newer, and Java 25.

Put the jar in the server's `mods` folder next to Fabric API and start the server once. It writes the config and,
with the world border on (the default), sets the border to 10,000 blocks across.

## Good to know

- Coming from the old 1.21.5 build: its death database is moved aside at startup, and the lockouts in it end.
- Read the [known limits](https://github.com/BobbyNooby/youonlylivetwice/blob/release/docs/known-limits.md) before you host.
